sentences.text: Shri Vaibhav Dubey, learned Counsel for the  appellant.
Shri Mukesh Parwal, learned Counsel for the  respondent/State.
A l s o h e a r d o n I . A . N o . 4 3 9 1 / 2 0 1 5 , w h i c h i s a n  application for grant of suspension of sentence regarding appellant Rafeeqe.
Counsel for the appellant has vehemently urged the fact that it was case of false implication.
Counsel submitted that the appellant was on bail and he has not misused the liberty granted  to him.

Counsel further submitted that a short sentence of six months' R.I.has  been imposed on the appellant for offence under Section 7(1), 7(3),(I)(II) r/w 16(I)A of  Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Counsel prayed that the application be  allowed since hearing of the appeal is likely to take a long time.
Counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the submissions put  forth by the Counsel for the appellant and prayed for dismissal of the application.

On considering the above submission, the impugned judgment and looking to the fact  that the appeal is likely to take a long time, I find that application I.A. No.4391/2015  needs to be allowed in the interest of justice and it is hereby allowed.

I t i s d i r e c t e d t h a t a p p e l l a n t b e r e l e a s e d o n b a i l  subject to his having paid the fine amount, if any, and on furnishing a personal bond of  Rs.25,000/(Rupees Twenty five thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the  satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before this Court/Registry on  2 7 / 7 / 2 0 1 5 a n d o n s u c h s u b s e q u e n t d a t e s a s m a y b e f i x e d i n t h i s  b e h a l f b y t h e o f f i c e . I n t h e m e a n w h i l e , t h e s u b s t a n t i v e  portion of the jail sentence shall remain suspended till hearing of the appeal.
(Mrs.S.R.Waghmare) Judge moni Ajay @ Babal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192125857/
